findings.finding: R1-1 is fixed as asked: the model pins each section's ids in order, the XR01/XR02 anchors and disjointness from v3's ids. A case's content under a pinned id is still free, though. CO02 repointed to ON47 (a binding the snapshot can see) with ON47's refusal was ACCEPTED (151 checks). So was CO03 repointed to ON01, and so was XR03 made a copy of XR02. CO02 and CO03 are the README's 'exact snapshots refused only by the lists', and they could drift into ordinary cases unnoticed. Cross-references give partial cover: editing ON48 or ON56 themselves is refused through CO02 or CO03.
findings.requiredChange: Optional hardening: pin the composed rows (id, snapshotCase, objectsCase) and the cross-version rows' base, or a digest of each case section, as model constants, as RB_ROWS_SHA256 does for the criteria. Not blocking.

findings.finding: RB07 matches a roleRef on kind == 'ClusterRole' and name == 'planeon:policy-observer'. Two invalid roleRef kinds naming the observer's ClusterRole pass: a lower-case 'clusterrole', and kind 'Role' in a ClusterRoleBinding. Neither can exist in a live cluster, because the apiserver's RBAC validation rejects both, and R10's producer refuses such a roleRef as Malformed (R99, MODEL_DEFINED.md:1531). So this is no live bypass. It is only a gap against RB07's own fail-closed wording, 'a roleRef ... that cannot be read refuses', since the model reads these roleRefs as valid instead of refusing them.
findings.requiredChange: Optional: refuse any other binding's roleRef whose kind is not ClusterRole (in a ClusterRoleBinding) or Role/ClusterRole (in a RoleBinding), as R99 does. Not blocking.

checks.check: RB07 (Q-RBAC-9 (a)): code, cases, coverage and bypass probes
checks.result: PASS, with R2-2. The decision's three negatives exist: a second ClusterRoleBinding (ON52 to system:authenticated, ON53), a RoleBinding referencing the ClusterRole (ON54, and ON55 without a roleRef apiGroup), and aggregated roles (ON56 empty selector, ON57 DoesNotExist, ON58 NotIn). ON59 (unknown operator) and ON60 (non-object roleRef) refuse as unreadable. OA05 (matchLabels, Exists, In, an empty selector list) and OA06 (a namespaced Role of the same name) are accepted. Both coverage rules refuse when their cases are removed; the generator's self-tests confirm this. My probes refused: a RoleBinding in kube-system; roleRef apiGroup example.com; a roleRef with an extra key; a null roleRef; the contract binding copied under another name; selectors {matchLabels: {}, matchExpressions: []}, {matchLabels: null, NotIn}, and a stock matchLabels selector followed by a NotIn selector; and malformed rules (a dict selector list, a list aggregationRule, operator 'notin', an unknown selector member). My probes accepted, correctly: matchLabels with NotIn in one selector, which needs a label; In and Exists only; Exists with DoesNotExist; a ClusterRole name differing in case; a namespaced Role of the same name. Accepted as a NOTE: invalid roleRef kinds (R2-2). The selector logic is right because the contract role has no labels (RB01), and an unlabeled object is matched only by a selector with no matchLabels whose expressions are all NotIn or DoesNotExist. The README's 'aggregation controller is required-disabled' cites I06 v1 README :129, which sits under 'Required-disabled controllers (SC06)' (:124).

Agree with both. (1) An aggregationRule with a null or empty clusterRoleSelectors list, an aggregationRule {} or an aggregationRule null is accepted: it selects nothing, upstream validation requires at least one selector anyway, and the aggregation controller is required-disabled. (2) A composed case pairs one snapshot case and one object case as given. The function cannot prove that the two come from one read; the caller obligation does that, and the README says so.
